country_overview: The United Kingdom operates a fully liberalised foreign-exchange regime with no general exchange controls since 1979. The framework is governed by the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) and HM Revenue & Customs (HMRC). There are no restrictions on current or capital account transactions for residents or non-residents.

summary.traveler: Travelers may bring in or take out unlimited amounts of foreign currency and British Pounds. No general currency declaration is required for normal travel amounts.
summary.business: Businesses and individuals enjoy full freedom to hold, transfer, convert and repatriate foreign currency through authorised banks and financial institutions.

rules.bring_foreign_currency_in: Foreign currency and sterling may be freely imported. Advance declaration of £10,000 or more can be made to Border Force up to 72 hours before travel; declaration at the border is also permitted.
rules.take_foreign_currency_out: Residents and non-residents may freely export currency and sterling documented as inbound or earned. Amounts of £10,000 or more require declaration. Non-residents may repatriate their full declared inbound currency.
rules.cash_declaration_threshold: No mandatory currency declaration threshold applies for ordinary travelers. Movements of €10,000 or more (or equivalent) in cash or bearer negotiable instruments must be declared to HMRC under anti-money laundering rules.
rules.resident_holding_rules: UK residents may hold and maintain foreign currency accounts freely with authorised banks and financial institutions.
rules.non_resident_rules: Non-residents may open and operate foreign currency accounts and transfer funds freely without prior approval.
rules.business_invoicing_settlement: Business transactions may be invoiced and settled in foreign currency or GBP. Cross-border payments and repatriation of funds are handled freely through authorised financial institutions.
rules.exchange_controls: The United Kingdom maintains no general exchange controls. The regime is fully liberalised for both current and capital account transactions.
rules.banking_conversion_practicality: Foreign exchange conversion and transfers are widely available through banks, licensed money exchange houses, and ATMs throughout the UK.
